note: Authenticated product execution of the exact native 4-ary 3-stage fly through BookSim's own `fly` network with `dest_tag_fly`. This is simulator evidence for the modeled fabric, not a hardware measurement and not a reference-benchmark result.

construction.attachment: asymmetric: terminal t injects at stage-0 router t//4 port t%4 and ejects at stage-2 router t//4 port t%4
construction.channel_id_law: stage * k**n + addr * k + port (BookSim KNFly::_OutChannel)
construction.router_id_law: stage * k**(n-1) + addr (BookSim KNFly::_BuildNet node counter)

static_first_hop_table.dialect: executed first-hop realization (deterministic; no legal-choice union needed)
static_first_hop_table.comparison: exact row equality AND exact port equality against the literal dest_tag_fly law
static_first_hop_table.note: The function answers every (router, destination node) pair, including pairs no real flow can occupy (a stage-2 router answering for a terminal that ejects elsewhere); the table is compared over all of them.

checks: every observed hop used the destination-tag port for (router, destination)
every flit's first observation is its own stage-0 injection router
every hop advanced exactly one stage
no flit appeared at a middle stage its digit class could not reach
every flit ejected at its own stage-2 router and nowhere else
every hop ran in the whole configured VC range

deadlock.argument: The CDG is built per destination terminal along that terminal's deterministic channel chain; every edge advances one stage, so acyclicity is a property of the construction rather than an assumption about it.

boundaries: modeled fabric evidence only; no energy, area or timing measurement
num_vcs = 1 in this workload's VC resource, so the destination-tag rule allocates the whole single-VC range
the generic stateless routing normalizer refuses FLY_DEST_TAG; the destination-indexed CDG is the deadlock proof
